# GitSecure

> GitSecure is the security mirror for GitHub. Take any public repo, swap
> `github.com` for `git-secure.com`, and get a plain-English security report
> — no install, no sign-up.
>
> `github.com/Squ1zM0/GitSecure` → `git-secure.com/Squ1zM0/GitSecure`

- Site: https://git-secure.com/
- Source: https://github.com/Squ1zM0/GitSecure
- Free to use. No sign-up, no login, no API key. Public repos only.

## What it does

Paste or type any public GitHub repo (`owner/repo`) and GitSecure returns a
plain-English security report: a score from 0–100 with a letter grade, counts,
a one-paragraph summary, and the full detail — file names, line numbers,
redacted secret fragments, framework versions, and vulnerability IDs with the
version that fixes each one. Every finding says what it is, what it lets an
attacker do, and the exact fix, in order.

It checks four things:

- **Leaked secrets** — Discord and Slack webhooks, AWS keys, GitHub tokens,
  Stripe and OpenAI keys, database URLs, private keys, committed `.env`
  files, hardcoded passwords. Checked in current files **and in full
  history** (newest-first). A secret deleted from HEAD but still in an old
  commit is still caught. Findings carry a triage annotation
  (`likely-test-key`, `likely-genuine-leak`, or `uncertain`); test keys
  deduct nothing from the score, uncertain findings half, genuine leaks
  in full, and the report shows the breakdown.
- **Frameworks** — what the repo is built with, with exact versions from
  lockfiles where possible: JS/TS (Next.js, React, Vue, Angular, Svelte,
  Vite, Express, Nest, Nuxt, Astro), Python (Django, Flask, FastAPI), Rust
  (Cargo / RustSec via OSV), Go (Gin, Echo, Fiber), Ruby (Rails, Sinatra),
  PHP (Laravel, Symfony, WordPress), Java/Kotlin (Spring Boot, Spring
  Framework, Kotlin), .NET (ASP.NET Core), plus Docker, Kubernetes,
  Terraform, GitHub Actions, Vercel and Supabase config. Unpinned (`*` /
  `latest`) versions are flagged; if a version cannot be determined, the
  report says so instead of guessing.
- **Dependency flaws** — known vulnerabilities in direct and transitive
  dependencies, checked against OSV.dev (a free public database of known
  software flaws; npm / PyPI / crates.io / Go / RubyGems / Packagist /
  Maven / NuGet), with full advisory detail (a plain summary, a severity
  score, and the version that fixes it) for every advisory found.
- **Security posture** — missing `SECURITY.md`, no Dependabot, `.gitignore`
  gaps, and risky GitHub Actions patterns (`pull_request_target`,
  `write-all`, secrets echoed into logs).

## What it does not do

- **Public repos only.** A missing or private repo returns a plain-English
  404 error, not a report.
- **Secrets are never shown in full** (fragment only: first 4 chars …
  last 2), **never stored**, and **never live-validated** (the scanner
  never calls the service a credential belongs to).
- **No sign-in flow, no owner verification, no stored reports.** Every
  scan is fresh and live; closing the page loses nothing, because a scan
  resumes from its cursor (see below).
- **Not a replacement for GitHub Advanced Security.** The site says so in
  its footer.

## How to use it

- **Web:** go to https://git-secure.com/ and enter `owner/repo`, or go
  straight to `https://git-secure.com/{owner}/{repo}` — for example
  https://git-secure.com/Squ1zM0/TechDirect
- **API:** `GET https://git-secure.com/api/scan/{owner}/{repo}` returns the
  full JSON report. A small repo answers 200 in one request; a large repo
  answers 202 with a cursor and the partial results so far — resume with
  `?cursor=...` on the same endpoint, or advance one chunk at a time with
  `POST /api/scan/chunk` (body `{ cursor, head?, historyFindings? }`).
  Errors carry honest statuses: 400 bad owner/repo format or bad cursor,
  404 repo not found or private, 409 repo changed mid-scan, 429 GitHub
  rate limit, 502 GitHub upstream error. There is no scan timeout.
- **MCP (for AI assistants):** canonical server URL
  `https://git-secure.com/mcp` (`/api/mcp` is an alias). Streamable HTTP,
  stateless, no sign-up, no API key. A plain `GET /mcp` is refused with a
  4xx — MCP clients use POST. Config snippet:
  `{ "mcpServers": { "gitsecure": { "url": "https://git-secure.com/mcp" } } }`

## MCP tools

- `scan_repo` (owner, repo) — run a live security scan, return the full report.
- `get_report` (owner, repo) — read or refresh the full report for a repo
  (runs a fresh live scan; reports are never stored).
- `resume_scan` (cursor) — continue a scan that is still running, from the
  cursor `scan_repo` or `get_report` returned.
- `list_checks` (no args) — what GitSecure checks, in plain English, plus
  the scan notes.

## Limits, stated honestly

- A scan takes about 15 seconds for a small repo; large repos run in
  chunks (HEAD first, then history newest-first, then assemble) and the
  caller resumes with a cursor. There is no file-count cap and no
  result-count cap: every file in the HEAD tree is scanned and every
  finding is listed.
- History is full, newest-first, to the oldest commit, via the git
  protocol first, then an ephemeral clone where a git binary exists, then
  the GitHub API. Only physical guards remain: a 500 MB streaming guard
  on the tarball download (tripping it switches to per-file fetches) and
  a 150 MB pack-download bound (past it, history goes through the API
  path instead). A history failure never fails the scan — the report
  carries a note and the HEAD scan still completes in full.
- **GitHub rate limits:** unauthenticated GitHub API is 60 requests/hour.
  A scan uses roughly 7 API calls plus raw file fetches, but the API
  history path uses about one request per commit, so a repo with more
  than ~50 commits can hit the unauthenticated limit; when it does, the
  scan keeps the findings so far and says so plainly. Setting a
  `GITHUB_TOKEN` server-side raises the limit to 5,000/hour.
- A very large repo (for example `torvalds/linux`, ~4 GB, ~1M commits)
  renders its HEAD report, but a full 1M-commit history walk takes a
  very long time even chunked. The scan says exactly how far it got; it
  does not fake completion.

## Known examples (from the project README and live verification, measured 2026-11-25/26)

- `Squ1zM0/TechDirect` scores 83/B with 2,802 files scanned.
- `DefinitelyTyped/DefinitelyTyped` scores 0/F with 403 secrets listed,
  61,814 files, 9,401 dependencies.
- Scanning GitSecure's own repo (`Squ1zM0/GitSecure`) returns 100/A
  (verified live 2026-11-26): 37 secret findings, all likely test keys
  (fixtures that deliberately bait the detectors), 0 vulnerabilities,
  0 posture issues. No real secret is in the repo.

## Optional

- `GITHUB_TOKEN` — a GitHub token raises the API rate limit from 60 to
  5,000 requests/hour. Server-side only, never in the repo. Without it,
  scans may hit the unauthenticated limit.
- No paid tier exists. No user counts or scan totals are published.
